headline: Southbury starter pack.
subhead: Six local spots to know around town. Swipe.

slides.title: Historic Main Street
slides.text: The long historic district runs along Route 6, featuring preserved colonial structures and long-standing town landmarks.

slides.title: Kettletown State Park
slides.text: Located along Lake Zoar, this park offers miles of wooded hiking trails and waterfront access.

slides.title: Pomperaug River
slides.text: This waterway winds through town, crossing beneath old bridges and alongside quiet conservation areas.

slides.title: Pratt Nature Center
slides.text: A community green space featuring preserved acreage, walking paths, and educational outdoor programs.

slides.title: Highway Access
slides.text: Interstate 84 runs directly through town, providing straightforward road connections toward Danbury and Waterbury.

slides.title: Annual Tree Lighting
slides.text: The town green hosts the traditional holiday tree lighting every winter as the colder weather sets in.

Getting to know Southbury CT takes time, especially once the November weather settles in. From the trails at Kettletown State Park to the historic buildings along Main Street, there are distinct landmarks that define the area. Interstate 84 makes the daily commute straightforward, while spots like the Pratt Nature Center offer quiet places to walk outside. With winter approaching, the town green is getting ready for traditional seasonal events.
